$comment: The CI allowlist of tests that FAIL ON TRUNK TODAY.
It exists so that `checks.yml` can be a hard gate on arrival instead of a
job that is red the day it lands -- a red-on-arrival gate teaches people to
ignore the gate, which is the failure mode this workflow was added to end.
It is NOT a way to skip or delete a test. Every entry here is still
COLLECTED AND RUN on every CI run, still reported as failing in the log, and
still counted. The allowlist only decides whether the JOB fails, and it
fails on ANY failure that is not named here.
It is also self-pruning: an entry whose test PASSES fails the job too, with
an instruction to delete the line. A known failure that quietly got fixed
must not stay on this list, because the list is the only thing standing
between the suite and a real regression sneaking in under a stale name.
Ids are `<classname>::<name>` exactly as the JUnit report spells them:
pytest writes a dotted module path; vitest writes the file path and the
full `describe > it` name.
Empty, and it stays empty. The one entry here was
tests.test_cumulative_support_outcomes::test_a_rejected_return_still_opens_no_work_item,
which raised `AttributeError: '_Runtime' object has no attribute
'patched'` because the module's workflow double never grew the method
`return_case_workflow.py` calls at lines 2247 and 2294. The double now
has it, and the same test uncovered a second staleness underneath: the
shipped release suspends `policy_evaluation`, so the rejected return it
names was never rejected. Both fixed on branch
feat/runtime-patch-double; the backend suite runs clean.
An empty list is the correct state and `assert_known_failures.py`
handles it: `allowed` is empty, so any failure at all is unexpected and
the job fails. Do not add an entry here to get a branch green.
The `/shipments` pair. `returns.session.read` is now visible from the
shipment console as well as /returns and /support, and the registry
test still pins the older two-domain set. Pre-existing on trunk; owned
by whoever settles whether the third domain is deliberate.
